options.reason: No liquid single-stock option market in Japan for this name. JPX option volume is concentrated in the index, so there is no event-implied move and no skew. Until 2026-09-18 that left priced_lean_pct as -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, which is ALSO the free control, so the baseline's lean and its own benchmark were the same number. They are no longer: `positioning` and `expected_move` below carry substitutes built from what Tokyo does publish, and this baseline supplies its own `priced_lean_pct` and `anchor_quality`.

history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. This is a cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a scale for how much this name moves, never as evidence about a particular past date.

event_plausibility.basis: issuer-notified date carried by JPX on the 決算発表予定日 sheet

positioning.basis: absent from the JPX register, so no disclosed position at or above the 0.5% threshold. A real zero, not missing data -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0.
positioning.margin_ratio_basis: 信用倍率, margin long balance / margin short balance, scraped from a broker portal rather than published by the exchange. Null is a normal outcome.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of twelve ESTIMATED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it, and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read researcher_japan/scripts/jp_priced_in.py, lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR, none is measured on Japanese data, and jp_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters today is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

evidence.text: This release carries the first 2027/8 (第51期) forecast, which includes Kobe Steel's exit from ON Building on 2027-03-31: the whole building, 4.1% of NLA, NOI about 1.24bn yen a year (3.1% on 39.9bn). The new tenant takes only 37% of the floor area from 2027-04-01, and the rest of its 68.3% phases in from 2027-10 to 2028-04. That leaves roughly 100-170 yen a unit of mechanical DPU drag against 1,795, unless the REIT draws on 4,216m yen (1,184 yen a unit) of internal reserve. It has done exactly that before: Kioicho in 2015 and Shiodome in 2021.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line is introduced at the October prints, when a new August-period forecast first appears. Those prints moved -0.59% (2022-10-19), -1.49% (2023-10-19), -2.88% (2024-10-23, the first print after Kobe Steel announced its move) and -0.63% (2025-10-23), next close against release-day close (Yahoo daily bars). The April 2026 print, which carried new leasing news (the Sunroute contract) and a 13.4% rise in NAV, moved +3.68%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The exit date and the new lease are public, but the DPU arithmetic for 2027/8 and whether reserves will cover it are not, because no period has been guided past 2027/2. If the drag were fully priced, the yield would already sit well above the J-REIT average. At 67,300 against a 3,628 yen annual DPU it yields 5.4%, at 0.74x NAV, which looks like a partial discount, not a full one.
evidence.independence: Reserve size and precedent from the 2026-04-22 investor presentation (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260422/140120260422508149.pdf, pp. 14 and 49). The vacancy timing is in the 2026-03-31 cancellation notice (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260331/140120260331594518.pdf). Same issuer, different documents.

evidence.text: The 2026/8 actual DPU will most likely land modestly above the 1,814 yen forecast. The REIT beat its latest forecast in each recent period (2025/8 1,854 against a 1,766 initial; 2026/2 1,837 against 1,791 revised). The hotel variable rents for this period are set on base months of Nov 2025 to May 2026, when Japan Hotel REIT reported H1 2026 RevPAR up 4.9%, against MTR's 100% YoY assumption. No 予想修正 was filed, so the result is within ±5%.
